audit_status.source_base: Hebrew source via Sefaria with source/English versification reconciliation; public-domain KJV familiar comparison
audit_status.review_note: Chapter 18 recounts Jehoshaphat's alliance with Ahab and the pivotal encounter with the prophet Micaiah, culminating in the battle of Ramoth-gilead where Ahab dies. The text presents a theologically complex narrative: divine sanction of deception through a lying spirit, prophetic integrity under pressure, and the mechanics of divine judgment. Sources align well; the narrative is substantially preserved between Kings 22 and Chronicles 18.

verses.restored: Jehoshaphat accumulated wealth and honor in great abundance, and he allied himself by marriage to Ahab.

familiar.text: Now Jehoshaphat had riches and honour in abundance, and joined affinity with Ahab.

notes.title: Alliance by marriage
notes.body: חתן (oath-binding kinship through marriage) signals political entanglement, not merely personal connection.

modern.text: Now Jehoshaphat had riches and honor in abundance, and he allied himself with Ahab by marriage.

original.text: וַיְהִ֧י לִֽיהוֹשָׁפָ֛ט עֹ֥שֶׁר וְכָב֖וֹד לָרֹ֑ב וַיִּתְחַתֵּ֖ן לְאַחְאָֽב

verses.restored: After some years he went down to Ahab in Samaria. Ahab slaughtered sheep and cattle for him in abundance, and for the people with him, and urged him to go up with him to Ramoth-gilead.

familiar.text: And after certain years he went down to Ahab to Samaria. And Ahab killed sheep and oxen for him in abundance, and for the people that he had with him, and persuaded him to go up with him to Ramothgilead.

notes.title: Persuasion through abundance
notes.body: The killing of animals and lavish feast are methods of political persuasion; Ahab seeks to seduce Jehoshaphat into dangerous alliance.

modern.text: And some years later he went down to visit Ahab in Samaria, where Ahab sacrificed many sheep and cattle for him and the people with him, and urged him to march up to Ramoth-gilead.

original.text: וַיֵּרֶד֩ לְקֵ֨ץ שָׁנִ֤ים אֶל אַחְאָב֙ לְשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן וַיִּֽזְבַּֽח ל֨וֹ אַחְאָ֜ב צֹ֤אן וּבָקָר֙ לָרֹ֔ב וְלָעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִמּ֑וֹ וַיְסִיתֵ֕הוּ לַעֲל֖וֹת אֶל רָמ֥וֹת גִּלְעָֽד

verses.restored: Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, Will you go with me to Ramoth-gilead? And he said to him, I am as you are, and my people as your people; with you we will be in the war.

familiar.text: And Ahab king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat king of Judah, Wilt thou go with me to Ramothgilead? And he answered him, I am as thou art, and my people as thy people; and we will be with thee in the war.

modern.text: Ahab king of Israel asked Jehoshaphat king of Judah, “Will you go with me against Ramoth-gilead?” And Jehoshaphat replied, “I am like you, and my people are your people; we will join you in the war.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֜אמֶר אַחְאָ֣ב מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֶל יְהֽוֹשָׁפָט֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה הֲתֵלֵ֥ךְ עִמִּ֖י רָמֹ֣ת גִּלְעָ֑ד וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ כָּמ֤וֹנִי כָמ֨וֹךָ֙ וּכְעַמְּךָ֣ עַמִּ֔י וְעִמְּךָ֖ בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה

verses.restored: And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, Inquire now at the word of YHWH.

familiar.text: And Jehoshaphat said unto the king of Israel, Enquire, I pray thee, at the word of the LORD to day.

notes.title: First appeal to divine word
notes.body: Jehoshaphat breaks ranks to demand prophetic consultation, a redemptive impulse within the dangerous alliance.

modern.text: But Jehoshaphat also said to the king of Israel, “Please inquire first for the word of the LORD.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט אֶל מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל דְּרָשׁ נָ֥א כַיּ֖וֹם אֶת דְּבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: So the king of Israel gathered the prophets—four hundred men—and said to them, Shall we go to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall I forbear? And they said, Go up, and YHWH will give it into the king's hand.

familiar.text: Therefore the king of Israel gathered together of prophets four hundred men, and said unto them, Shall we go to Ramothgilead to battle, or shall I forbear? And they said, Go up; for God will deliver it into the king’s hand.

notes.title: Institutional prophecy
notes.body: The 400 prophets represent state-sanctioned religious authority, likely prophets of other deities rather than YHWH-prophets.

modern.text: So the king of Israel assembled the prophets, four hundred men, and asked them, “Should we go to war against Ramoth-gilead, or should we refrain?” “Go up,” they replied, “and God will deliver it into the hand of the king.”

original.text: וַיִּקְבֹּ֨ץ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל אֶֽת הַנְּבִאִים֮ אַרְבַּ֣ע מֵא֣וֹת אִישׁ֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם הֲנֵלֵ֞ךְ אֶל רָמֹ֥ת גִּלְעָ֛ד לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אִם אֶחְדָּ֑ל וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ עֲלֵ֔ה וְיִתֵּ֥ן הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּיַ֥ד הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: And Jehoshaphat said, Is there not here still a prophet of YHWH, that we might inquire of him?

familiar.text: But Jehoshaphat said, Is there not here a prophet of the LORD besides, that we might enquire of him?

notes.title: Prophetic integrity
notes.body: Jehoshaphat's skepticism about institutional prophecy drives him to seek an independent prophet.

modern.text: But Jehoshaphat asked, “Is there not still a prophet of the LORD here of whom we can inquire?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יְה֣וֹשָׁפָ֔ט הַאֵ֨ין פֹּ֥ה נָבִ֛יא לַיהוָ֖ה ע֑וֹד וְנִדְרְשָׁ֖ה מֵאֹתֽוֹ

verses.restored: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, There is yet one man by whom we might inquire of YHWH, but I hate him, for he never prophesies good to me, but always evil—Micaiah son of Imlah. And Jehoshaphat said, Let not the king speak thus.

familiar.text: And the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, There is yet one man, by whom we may enquire of the LORD: but I hate him; for he never prophesied good unto me, but always evil: the same is Micaiah the son of Imla. And Jehoshaphat said, Let not the king say so.

notes.title: Prophetic unpopularity
notes.body: Ahab's contempt for Micaiah demonstrates how true prophecy antagonizes those in power who seek confirmation rather than truth.

modern.text: The king of Israel answered, “There is still one man who can ask the LORD, but I hate him because he never prophesies anything good for me, but only bad. He is Micaiah son of Imlah.” “The king should not say that!” Jehoshaphat replied.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל אֶֽל יְהוֹשָׁפָ֡ט ע֣וֹד אִישׁ אֶחָ֡ד לִדְרוֹשׁ֩ אֶת יְהוָ֨ה מֵֽאֹת֜וֹ וַאֲנִ֣י שְׂנֵאתִ֗יהוּ כִּֽי אֵ֠ינֶנּוּ מִתְנַבֵּ֨א עָלַ֤י לְטוֹבָה֙ כִּ֣י כָל יָמָ֣יו לְרָעָ֔ה ה֖וּא מִיכָ֣יְהוּ בֶן יִמְלָ֑א וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יְה֣וֹשָׁפָ֔ט אַל יֹאמַ֥ר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ כֵּֽן

verses.restored: So the king of Israel called one of his eunuchs and said, Fetch quickly Micaiah son of Imlah.

familiar.text: And the king of Israel called for one of his officers, and said, Fetch quickly Micaiah the son of Imla.

modern.text: So the king of Israel called one of his officials and said, “Bring Micaiah son of Imlah at once.”

original.text: וַיִּקְרָא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל סָרִ֖יס אֶחָ֑ד וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מַהֵ֖ר מיכהו בֶן יִמְלָֽא

verses.restored: Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah sat each on his throne, clothed in their robes, in an open place at the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets prophesied before them.

familiar.text: And the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah sat either of them on his throne, clothed in their robes, and they sat in a void place at the entering in of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets prophesied before them.

notes.title: Visual staging
notes.body: The throne-sitting and robing establish official authority and expectation. The 'open place' (goren, threshing floor) suggests both exposure and theatricality.

modern.text: Dressed in royal attire, the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting on their thrones at the threshing floor by the entrance of the gate of Samaria, with all the prophets prophesying before them.

original.text: וּמֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל וִֽיהוֹשָׁפָ֣ט מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֡ה יוֹשְׁבִים֩ אִ֨ישׁ עַל כִּסְא֜וֹ מְלֻבָּשִׁ֤ים בְּגָדִים֙ וְיֹשְׁבִ֣ים בְּגֹ֔רֶן פֶּ֖תַח שַׁ֣עַר שֹׁמְר֑וֹן וְכָל הַ֨נְּבִיאִ֔ים מִֽתְנַבְּאִ֖ים לִפְנֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: And Zedekiah son of Chenaanah had made himself horns of iron and said, Thus says YHWH: With these you will gore Aram until they are consumed.

familiar.text: And Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah had made him horns of iron, and said, Thus saith the LORD, With these thou shalt push Syria until they be consumed.

notes.title: Symbolic prophecy
notes.body: Iron horns as symbols of military strength and aggressive conquest; Zedekiah performs the prophecy.

modern.text: Now Zedekiah son of Chenaanah had made for himself iron horns and declared, “This is what the LORD says: ‘With these you shall gore the Arameans until they are finished off.’”

original.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ ל֛וֹ צִדְקִיָּ֥הוּ בֶֽן כְּנַעֲנָ֖ה קַרְנֵ֣י בַרְזֶ֑ל וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בְּאֵ֛לֶּה תְּנַגַּ֥ח אֶת אֲרָ֖ם עַד כַּלּוֹתָֽם

verses.restored: And all the prophets prophesied thus, saying, Go up to Ramoth-gilead and prosper, and YHWH will give it into the hand of the king.

familiar.text: And all the prophets prophesied so, saying, Go up to Ramothgilead, and prosper: for the LORD shall deliver it into the hand of the king.

modern.text: And all the prophets were prophesying the same, saying, “Go up to Ramoth-gilead and prosper, for the LORD will deliver it into the hand of the king.” Micaiah Prophesies against Ahab (1 Kings 22:13–28)

original.text: וְכָל הַ֨נְּבִאִ֔ים נִבְּאִ֥ים כֵּ֖ן לֵאמֹ֑ר עֲלֵ֞ה רָמֹ֤ת גִּלְעָד֙ וְהַצְלַ֔ח וְנָתַ֥ן יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַ֥ד הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Now the messenger who had gone to summon Micaiah spoke to him, saying, Behold, the words of the prophets declare good to the king with one mouth; let your word, please, be like one of theirs, and speak good.

familiar.text: And the messenger that went to call Micaiah spake to him, saying, Behold, the words of the prophets declare good to the king with one assent; let thy word therefore, I pray thee, be like one of theirs, and speak thou good.

notes.title: Prophetic pressure
notes.body: The messenger offers Micaiah the invitation to compromise—to align with institutional prophecy and gain favor.

modern.text: Then the messenger who had gone to call Micaiah instructed him, “Behold, with one accord the words of the prophets are favorable to the king. So please let your words be like theirs, and speak favorably.”

original.text: וְהַמַּלְאָ֞ךְ אֲשֶׁר הָלַ֣ךְ לִקְרֹ֣א לְמִיכָ֗יְהוּ דִּבֶּ֤ר אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּ֞ה דִּבְרֵ֧י הַנְּבִאִ֛ים פֶּֽה אֶחָ֥ד ט֖וֹב אֶל הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וִֽיהִי נָ֧א דְבָרְךָ֛ כְּאַחַ֥ד מֵהֶ֖ם וְדִבַּ֥רְתָּ טּֽוֹב

verses.restored: And Micaiah said, As YHWH lives, surely what my God says, that I will speak.

familiar.text: And Micaiah said, As the LORD liveth, even what my God saith, that will I speak.

notes.title: Prophetic oath
notes.body: Micaiah's invocation of YHWH's life affirms that his allegiance is to divine word, not royal preference.

modern.text: But Micaiah said, “As surely as the LORD lives, I will speak whatever my God tells me.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מִיכָ֑יְהוּ חַי יְהוָ֕ה כִּ֛י אֶת אֲשֶׁר יֹאמַ֥ר אֱלֹהַ֖י אֹת֥וֹ אֲדַבֵּֽר

verses.restored: And when he came to the king, the king said to him, Micaiah, shall we go to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall I forbear? And he said, Go up and prosper, and they will be given into your hand.

familiar.text: And when he was come to the king, the king said unto him, Micaiah, shall we go to Ramothgilead to battle, or shall I forbear? And he said, Go ye up, and prosper, and they shall be delivered into your hand.

notes.title: Prophetic irony
notes.body: Micaiah mirrors the false prophets' words, but the context reveals them as doom, not blessing. The repetition exposes the gap between what is said and what is true.

modern.text: When Micaiah arrived, the king asked him, “Micaiah, should we go to war against Ramoth-gilead, or should we refrain?” “Go up and triumph,” Micaiah replied, “for they will be given into your hand.”

original.text: וַיָּבֹא֮ אֶל הַמֶּלֶךְ֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֵלָ֗יו מִיכָה֙ הֲנֵלֵ֞ךְ אֶל רָמֹ֥ת גִּלְעָ֛ד לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אִם אֶחְדָּ֑ל וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ עֲל֣וּ וְהַצְלִ֔יחוּ וְיִנָּתְנ֖וּ בְּיֶדְכֶֽם

verses.restored: And the king said to him, How many times must I adjure you to speak to me only truth in the name of YHWH?

familiar.text: And the king said to him, How many times shall I adjure thee that thou say nothing but the truth to me in the name of the LORD?

notes.title: Adjuration
notes.body: The king's oath-formula demands that Micaiah speak truth, not flattery—a demand that seals the king's own doom.

modern.text: But the king said to him, “How many times must I make you swear not to tell me anything but the truth in the name of the LORD?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַד כַּמֶּ֥ה פְעָמִ֖ים אֲנִ֣י מַשְׁבִּיעֶ֑ךָ אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא תְדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֛י רַק אֱמֶ֖ת בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Then he said, I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains like sheep without a shepherd; and YHWH said, These have no lord. Let each return to his house in peace.

familiar.text: Then he said, I did see all Israel scattered upon the mountains, as sheep that have no shepherd: and the LORD said, These have no master; let them return therefore every man to his house in peace.

notes.title: Vision of defeat
notes.body: The scattered sheep image reverses expectations of victory. 'No lord' (אדונים) may denote kingship or divine guidance; the absence is total.

modern.text: So Micaiah declared: “I saw all Israel scattered on the hills like sheep without a shepherd. And the LORD said, ‘These people have no master; let each one return home in peace.’”

original.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר רָאִ֤יתִי אֶת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נְפוֹצִ֣ים עַל הֶֽהָרִ֔ים כַּצֹּ֕אן אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵין לָהֶ֖ן רֹעֶ֑ה וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ לֹֽא אֲדֹנִ֣ים לָאֵ֔לֶּה יָשׁ֥וּבוּ אִישׁ לְבֵית֖וֹ בְּשָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, Did I not tell you that he would not prophesy good to me, but evil?

familiar.text: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, Did I not tell thee that he would not prophesy good unto me, but evil?

modern.text: Then the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “Did I not tell you that he never prophesies good for me, but only bad?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל יְהוֹשָׁפָ֑ט הֲלֹא֙ אָמַ֣רְתִּי אֵלֶ֔יךָ לֹא יִתְנַבֵּ֥א עָלַ֛י ט֖וֹב כִּ֥י אִם לְרָֽע

verses.restored: And he said, Therefore hear the word of YHWH: I saw YHWH sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by his right and by his left.

familiar.text: Again he said, Therefore hear the word of the LORD; I saw the LORD sitting upon his throne, and all the host of heaven standing on his right hand and on his left.

notes.title: Heavenly throne vision
notes.body: Micaiah claims direct visionary access to YHWH's council and throne, establishing his prophecy as originating from the divine assembly.

modern.text: Micaiah continued, “Therefore hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting on His throne, and all the host of heaven standing on His right and on His left.

original.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לָכֵ֖ן שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֑ה רָאִ֤יתִי אֶת יְהוָה֙ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב עַל כִּסְא֔וֹ וְכָל צְבָ֤א הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ עֹֽמְדִ֔ים עַל יְמִינ֖וֹ וּשְׂמֹאלֽוֹ

verses.restored: And YHWH said, Who will entice Ahab king of Israel, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead? And one said this thing, and another said that.

familiar.text: And the LORD said, Who shall entice Ahab king of Israel, that he may go up and fall at Ramothgilead? And one spake saying after this manner, and another saying after that manner.

notes.title: Divine deliberation
notes.body: YHWH solicits proposals from the heavenly council for how to lure Ahab to his death. The process reveals judgment as relational, not mechanical.

modern.text: And the LORD said, ‘Who will entice Ahab king of Israel to march up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?’ And one suggested this, and another that.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה מִ֤י יְפַתֶּה֙ אֶת אַחְאָ֣ב מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְיַ֕עַל וְיִפֹּ֖ל בְּרָמ֣וֹת גִּלְעָ֑ד וַיֹּ֕אמֶר זֶ֚ה אֹמֵ֣ר כָּ֔כָה וְזֶ֖ה אֹמֵ֥ר כָּֽכָה

verses.restored: Then a spirit came forth and stood before YHWH and said, I will entice him. And YHWH said to him, By what means?

familiar.text: Then there came out a spirit, and stood before the LORD, and said, I will entice him. And the LORD said unto him, Wherewith?

notes.title: The spirit's self-offering
notes.body: A spirit from the heavenly council volunteers for the work of deception. YHWH's question seeks specification, not moral justification.

modern.text: Then a spirit came forward, stood before the LORD, and said, ‘I will entice him.’ ‘By what means?’ asked the LORD.

original.text: וַיֵּצֵ֣א הָר֗וּחַ וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֲנִ֣י אֲפַתֶּ֑נּוּ וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה אֵלָ֖יו בַּמָּֽה

verses.restored: And he said, I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And YHWH said, You will entice him, and also prevail. Go out and do this.

familiar.text: And he said, I will go out, and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And the Lord said, Thou shalt entice him, and thou shalt also prevail: go out, and do even so.

notes.title: Divine authorization of deception
notes.body: YHWH explicitly commissions the lying spirit to work through the prophets' mouths. This is not demonic subversion but divine use of spiritual agency for judgment.

modern.text: And he replied, ‘I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets.’ ‘You will surely entice him and prevail,’ said the LORD. ‘Go and do it.’

original.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֵצֵא֙ וְהָיִ֨יתִי֙ לְר֣וּחַ שֶׁ֔קֶר בְּפִ֖י כָּל נְבִיאָ֑יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר תְּפַתֶּה֙ וְגַם תּוּכָ֔ל צֵ֖א וַעֲשֵׂה כֵֽן

verses.restored: So now, behold, YHWH has put a lying spirit in the mouth of these prophets of yours, and YHWH has spoken evil against you.

familiar.text: Now therefore, behold, the LORD hath put a lying spirit in the mouth of these thy prophets, and the LORD hath spoken evil against thee.

notes.title: Interpretation of false prophecy
notes.body: Micaiah reveals that the false prophets' words are not mere human error but divinely-permitted deception functioning as judgment against Ahab.

modern.text: So you see, the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouths of these prophets of yours, and the LORD has pronounced disaster against you.”

original.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה הִנֵּ֨ה נָתַ֤ן יְהוָה֙ ר֣וּחַ שֶׁ֔קֶר בְּפִ֖י נְבִיאֶ֣יךָ אֵ֑לֶּה וַֽיהוָ֔ה דִּבֶּ֥ר עָלֶ֖יךָ רָעָֽה

verses.restored: Then Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came near and struck Micaiah on the cheek and said, Which way did the spirit of YHWH go from me to speak to you?

familiar.text: Then Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah came near, and smote Micaiah upon the cheek, and said, Which way went the Spirit of the LORD from me to speak unto thee?

notes.title: Prophetic conflict
notes.body: Zedekiah's physical violence against Micaiah is both defense of false prophecy and implicit acknowledgment that truth threatens his authority.

modern.text: Then Zedekiah son of Chenaanah went up, struck Micaiah in the face, and demanded, “Which way did the Spirit of the LORD go when He departed from me to speak with you?”

original.text: וַיִּגַּשׁ֙ צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ בֶֽן כְּנַעֲנָ֔ה וַיַּ֥ךְ אֶת מִיכָ֖יְהוּ עַל הַלֶּ֑חִי וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֵ֣י זֶ֤ה הַדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ עָבַ֧ר רֽוּחַ יְהוָ֛ה מֵאִתִּ֖י לְדַבֵּ֥ר אֹתָֽךְ

verses.restored: And Micaiah said, Behold, you will see on that day when you go into an inner chamber to hide yourself.

familiar.text: And Micaiah said, Behold, thou shalt see on that day when thou shalt go into an inner chamber to hide thyself.

notes.title: Prophetic judgment
notes.body: Micaiah's response predicts Zedekiah's humiliation—not physical death but the exposure of his false prophecy and his retreat from public view.

modern.text: Micaiah replied, “You will soon see, on that day when you go and hide in an inner room.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מִיכָ֔יְהוּ הִנְּךָ֥ רֹאֶ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא אֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּב֛וֹא חֶ֥דֶר בְּחֶ֖דֶר לְהֵחָבֵֽא

verses.restored: And the king of Israel said, Take Micaiah and send him back to Amon the governor of the city and to Joash the king's son,

familiar.text: Then the king of Israel said, Take ye Micaiah, and carry him back to Amon the governor of the city, and to Joash the king’s son;

notes.title: Micaiah's arrest
notes.body: Amon (governor, šar) and Joash (royal prince) form a supervisory apparatus designed to keep the prophet under control.

modern.text: And the king of Israel declared, “Take Micaiah and return him to Amon the governor of the city and to Joash the king’s son,

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל קְחוּ֙ אֶת מִיכָ֔יְהוּ וַהֲשִׁיבֻ֖הוּ אֶל אָמ֣וֹן שַׂר הָעִ֑יר וְאֶל יוֹאָ֖שׁ בֶּן הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: and say, Thus says the king: Put this man in prison and feed him with the bread of affliction and the water of affliction, until I come back in peace.

familiar.text: And say, Thus saith the king, Put this fellow in the prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and with water of affliction, until I return in peace.

notes.title: Prophetic imprisonment
notes.body: Minimal rations of bread and water (standard in ancient Near Eastern imprisonment) are explicitly designed as punishment for Micaiah's inconvenient prophecy.

modern.text: and tell them that this is what the king says: ‘Put this man in prison and feed him only bread and water until I return safely.’”

original.text: וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֗ם כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ שִׂ֥ימוּ זֶ֖ה בֵּ֣ית הַכֶּ֑לֶא וְהַאֲכִלֻ֜הוּ לֶ֤חֶם לַ֨חַץ֙ וּמַ֣יִם לַ֔חַץ עַ֖ד שׁוּבִ֥י בְשָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: And Micaiah said, If you return in peace, then YHWH has not spoken by me. And he said, Hear, all you peoples.

familiar.text: And Micaiah said, If thou certainly return in peace, then hath not the LORD spoken by me. And he said, Hearken, all ye people.

notes.title: Prophetic self-attestation
notes.body: Micaiah makes his continued life conditional on his prophecy's truth. He summons public witness ('all peoples,' עמים כלם) to the judgment about to unfold.

modern.text: But Micaiah replied, “If you ever return safely, the LORD has not spoken through me.” Then he added, “Take heed, all you people!” Ahab’s Defeat and Death (1 Kings 22:29–40)

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מִיכָ֔יְהוּ אִם שׁ֤וֹב תָּשׁוּב֙ בְּשָׁל֔וֹם לֹא דִבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בִּ֑י וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁמְע֖וּ עַמִּ֥ים כֻּלָּֽם

verses.restored: So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.

familiar.text: So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah went up to Ramothgilead.

modern.text: So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.

original.text: וַיַּ֧עַל מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וִֽיהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֖ה אֶל רָמֹ֥ת גִּלְעָֽד

verses.restored: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, I will disguise myself and go into the battle, but you put on your robes. So the king of Israel disguised himself, and they went into the battle.

familiar.text: And the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, I will disguise myself, and will go to the battle; but put thou on thy robes. So the king of Israel disguised himself; and they went to the battle.

notes.title: Strategic disguise
notes.body: Ahab's disguise is both military tactic (to avoid enemy focus) and ironic irony given Micaiah's prophecy. Jehoshaphat, wearing royal garb, becomes the visible target.

modern.text: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “I will disguise myself and go into battle, but you wear your royal robes.” So the king of Israel disguised himself and went into battle.

original.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶל יְהוֹשָׁפָ֗ט הִתְחַפֵּשׂ֙ וָב֣וֹא בַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְאַתָּ֖ה לְבַ֣שׁ בְּגָדֶ֑יךָ וַיִּתְחַפֵּשׂ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה

verses.restored: Now the king of Aram had commanded the captains of the chariots with him, saying, Fight not with small or great, save only with the king of Israel.

familiar.text: Now the king of Syria had commanded the captains of the chariots that were with him, saying, Fight ye not with small or great, save only with the king of Israel.

notes.title: Aramean strategy
notes.body: Ben-Hadad (named in Kings 22:31) instructs his chariot commanders to focus solely on the king of Israel, reflecting both military logic and recognition of Ahab's centrality.

modern.text: Now the king of Aram had ordered his chariot commanders, “Do not fight with anyone, small or great, except the king of Israel.”

original.text: וּמֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֡ם צִוָּה֩ אֶת שָׂרֵ֨י הָרֶ֤כֶב אֲשֶׁר לוֹ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֚א תִּלָּ֣חֲמ֔וּ אֶת הַקָּטֹ֖ן אֶת הַגָּד֑וֹל כִּ֛י אִֽם אֶת מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְבַדּֽוֹ

verses.restored: And when the chariot captains saw Jehoshaphat, they said, This is the king of Israel. And they turned to fight against him. But Jehoshaphat cried out, and YHWH helped him; and God turned them away from him.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, that they said, It is the king of Israel. Therefore they compassed about him to fight: but Jehoshaphat cried out, and the LORD helped him; and God moved them to depart from him.

notes.title: Providential protection
notes.body: Jehoshaphat's deliverance from Aramean forces is attributed directly to YHWH's intervention. He cries out, YHWH responds, and God turns the enemy away—a reversal of Ahab's trajectory.

modern.text: When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, “This is the king of Israel!” So they turned to fight against him, but Jehoshaphat cried out, and the LORD helped him. God drew them away from him.

original.text: וַיְהִ֡י כִּרְאוֹת֩ שָׂרֵ֨י הָרֶ֜כֶב אֶת יְהוֹשָׁפָ֗ט וְהֵ֤מָּה אָֽמְרוּ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל ה֔וּא וַיָּסֹ֥בּוּ עָלָ֖יו לְהִלָּחֵ֑ם וַיִּזְעַ֤ק יְהֽוֹשָׁפָט֙ וַֽיהוָ֣ה עֲזָר֔וֹ וַיְסִיתֵ֥ם אֱלֹהִ֖ים מִמֶּֽנּוּ

verses.restored: And when the chariot captains saw that it was not the king of Israel, they turned back from pursuing him.

familiar.text: For it came to pass, that, when the captains of the chariots perceived that it was not the king of Israel, they turned back again from pursuing him.

modern.text: And when the chariot commanders saw that he was not the king of Israel, they turned back from pursuing him.

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י כִּרְאוֹת֙ שָׂרֵ֣י הָרֶ֔כֶב כִּ֥י לֹא הָיָ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ מֵאַחֲרָֽיו

verses.restored: And a certain man drew his bow at random and struck the king of Israel between the segments and the breastplate. And he said to the charioteer, Turn your hand and carry me out of the camp, for I am wounded.

familiar.text: And a certain man drew a bow at a venture, and smote the king of Israel between the joints of the harness: therefore he said to his chariot man, Turn thine hand, that thou mayest carry me out of the host; for I am wounded.

notes.title: Ahab's wounding
notes.body: The 'random' arrow (לתמו, at his luck/chance) strikes between armor plates—a gap where protection ends. The wound is fatal but slow. Ahab directs his charioteer to remove him from combat.

modern.text: However, a certain man drew his bow without taking special aim, and he struck the king of Israel between the joints of his armor. So the king said to his charioteer, “Turn around and take me out of the battle, for I am badly wounded!”

original.text: וְאִ֗ישׁ מָשַׁ֤ךְ בַּקֶּ֨שֶׁת֙ לְתֻמּ֔וֹ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בֵּ֥ין הַדְּבָקִ֖ים וּבֵ֣ין הַשִּׁרְיָ֑ן וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָֽרַכָּ֗ב הֲפֹ֧ךְ ידיך וְהוֹצֵאתַ֥נִי מִן הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה כִּ֥י הָחֳלֵֽיתִי

verses.restored: And the battle mounted that day, and the king of Israel propped himself up in his chariot facing Aram until the evening, and he died at the time the sun was setting.

familiar.text: And the battle increased that day: howbeit the king of Israel stayed himself up in his chariot against the Syrians until the even: and about the time of the sun going down he died.

notes.title: Ahab's death
notes.body: Ahab maintains position in the chariot through the long battle, using it as a position to command or hide. He dies at sunset, fulfilling Micaiah's prophecy of his fall at Ramoth-gilead.

modern.text: The battle raged throughout that day, and the king of Israel propped himself up in his chariot facing the Arameans until evening. And at sunset he died.

original.text: וַתַּ֤עַל הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וּמֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הָיָ֨ה מַעֲמִ֧יד בַּמֶּרְכָּבָ֛ה נֹ֥כַח אֲרָ֖ם עַד הָעָ֑רֶב וַיָּ֕מָת לְעֵ֖ת בּ֥וֹא הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ

translation_notes: Divine deception narrative (vv. 18–22) is presented directly without harmonization; the lying spirit operates within YHWH's sovereign purposes.
Micaiah's name appears in variant form in v. 8 (likely scribal variation; both reference the same figure).
The Aramean king remains unnamed in Chronicles (contrast with 1 Kings 22).
safety_note: Chapter contains royal political manipulation, false prophecy sanctioned by divine decree, violent conflict, and the death of a king in battle. Does not sanitize moral complexity.
source_witness_audit_flags: Variant spelling of Micaiah in v. 8; compare textual witnesses.
Verse 33 contains emended text (ידיך vs. יָדְךָ); preserved as likely scribal variant.
